news.title: PREVIEW: Junior Football Ferns to be tested at FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: New Zealand’s Junior Football Ferns face a tough test when they represent their country at the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup, starting in Poland this weekend. The cities of Łódź, Katowice, Sosnowiec, and Bielsko-Biała will share the 24-team tournament. New Zealand will be represented for the tenth time. The top two teams in each group and the best four third-placed teams will advance to the knockout rounds, but the Junior Football Ferns will have quite the task in an unforgiving Group D.

news.title: Luka Modric Continues International Odyssey: From World Cup Highlights to Nations League Challenges
news.lede: Croatian football star Luka Modric is set to extend his illustrious international career beyond the FIFA World Cup, having announced his availability for the UEFA Nations League fixtures against Czechia, World Cup champions Spain, and England. This confirmation came from the Croatian Football Federation on Saturday. The federation's official X handle declared, "#Croatia captain @lukamodric10 is back for the #NationsLeague clashes with Czechia, Spain, and England! Modrić's commitment to head coach Slaven Bilić and HNS president Marijan Kustić underlines his readiness to enhance Croatia's international standing, with 202 caps underscoring his iconic status."

news.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino makes an appearance at U20 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has arrived at the opening of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup as he faces continuing pressure since abandoning his plan to sell off World Cup profits. Infantino was seen in the stands speaking with Polish football federation president Cezary Kulesza as host nation Poland faced Argentina on the opening day of the tournament on Saturday. Infantino had mostly kept out of the spotlight in the weeks since his World Cup sell-off plan fell apart amid opposition from many Fifa member nations and some of his own officials. The European nations – a quarter of the 24-team field – backed down on a boycott threat last week, citing assurances from Fifa that the plan would not be revived.
